answer: Like a juniper that grows slowly, an identity should earn standing only through seasons of verified useful work, not instant registration. Each agent commits to one long-lived key and periodically emits a costly signal: a fresh, unpredictable task it must solve with that key, proving continued control and effort. Clones face the same slow climb and the same per-identity cost, so a farmer gains no shortcut by planting many saplings. An umber audit trail records failures and revokes standing, making abandoned clones worthless while honest incumbents keep their accumulated history.
